population.definition: every anchor galaxy with a defined position angle

spiral_armed.definition: has-spiral-arms vote fraction above 0.5; the chiral pool

smooth.definition: smooth vote fraction above 0.7; achiral, the population control

edge_on.definition: edge-on vote fraction above 0.5; discs whose handedness is not resolvable

all.definition: every galaxy with a defined position angle

population.note: the operator needs a fitted major axis, so the population is pa_defined rather than the elongated cut of Diagnostics 1 and 2

operator.isolating: major_axis_flip: rotate the major axis horizontal, flip, rotate back
operator.control: axis_sandwich: the same two rotations with the flip omitted
verified_properties: turns a synthetic spiral into its independently built mirror twin
leaves an achiral ellipse unchanged beyond the two rotations
preserves the envelope axis and the ellipticity
is an involution when compared against the control applied twice
carries the same interpolation loss as the control

d_spec.definition: E(x) - E(majorflip(x)), the scoping document's definition

EXTENSION_d_pure.definition: E(sandwich(x)) - E(majorflip(x)); both sides carry identical resampling, so this is chirality alone

NULL_d_resampling.definition: E(x) - E(sandwich(x)); the same procedure with a rotation instead of a flip, so it carries the resampling and no parity inversion

EXTENSION_confound_budget.question: the scoping document compares spiral against smooth magnitudes and calls the smooth value the interpolation floor. That floor is not shared: resampling damages fine structure more, so the featured pool loses more from the rotations alone
EXTENSION_confound_budget.reading: a ratio above 1 in the resampling row is the confound measured directly; the d_pure row is the same comparison with that confound removed

axis_statistic_calibration.reading: the first two cases both give a dominant leading axis; they are separated by the sign balance and the mean-to-median ratio, not by the leading fraction

NULL_random_direction_variance_fraction.note: a random direction captures 1/d of the variance in expectation

spiral_armed.reading: a dominant leading axis is NOT on its own evidence of encoded handedness. A constant offset shared by every object, which is what a systematic resampling residual looks like, produces an equally dominant axis. Verified on synthetic data: a true handedness axis gives sign_balance near 0.5 and mean_vector_norm_over_median_norm near 0, while a common offset gives sign balance 1.0 and a ratio near 1. The three fields must be read together

EXTENSION_axis_separation.expectation: near zero if the flip and the resampling write to different directions; near one would mean the chirality axis is resampling

EXTENSION_orientation_leak.question: the operator preserves the envelope axis exactly but reflects a chiral object's moment angle about it. If the model's angle readout follows the moments rather than the envelope, orientation leaks into the difference vector for chiral objects and only for them
EXTENSION_orientation_leak.probe: the Diagnostic 1 doubled-angle probe, fit once on untransformed embeddings
EXTENSION_orientation_leak.reading: a shift near zero everywhere means the readout follows the envelope and no orientation leaks; a shift larger in the chiral pools than in the smooth pool is the leak, and bounds how much of d is orientation

EXTENSION_ellipticity_grading.note: the flip is about the CATALOG major axis, whose uncertainty grows as the object becomes round, so the operator isolates chirality less cleanly at low ellipticity

sign_test.null: half the pairs positive if the flip moved both members equally

EXTENSION_matched_control.reading: the paired difference is the excess displacement of a spiral over an otherwise identical smooth galaxy. The resampling row is the same comparison for the operation that inverts nothing, on the same pairs, so any residual mismatch in size or brightness would move both rows together. It is what the chirality row has to beat

EXTENSION_arms_versus_featured.reading: edge-on discs carry arms that cannot be resolved as handedness, so the physics predicts they behave like the achiral pool despite being discs
